# A calm copper coupon does not clear silver

> **Direct Answer Block**: Why a passing G1 copper corrosion coupon (<300 A/30d) never clears a data hall for RoHS lead-free servers without a paired silver coupon (<200 A/30d). In mission-critical data center commissioning and operations, engineers enforce this boundary using deterministic physical equations, calibrated field instrumentation, and auditable sign-off gates rather than relying on vendor brochure summaries, uncalibrated software plots, or verbal assurances. Every measurement and state transition must be recorded with synchronized UTC timestamps and explicit pass/fail thresholds before a signature is granted.

![Read both metals, or do not claim the joints.](figures/flagship/fig-02-isa-71-04-severity-classification-matrix.png)

Gas corrosion on boards is not dust, and it is not rust in a water pipe. Lead-free finishes put silver at the joint. Gases that attack silver can open that joint while copper in the same room still looks acceptable. A pass on copper alone is not a pass for the joints.

Hang both metals, or write that silver was not measured and you will not claim the joints. A report that collapses the pair into one class has hidden the split. Ask for the two reads. If they cannot be separated, you do not know which sentence you have.

The coupon does not name the gas, and it does not date a board failure. Smell, a particle count, and a photograph of a tarnished connector are not rates. File them on other lines. Do not staple a chilled-water iron trend to this sheet and call it one story.

A class is a word the lab report may print beside an edition it cites. Do not reconstruct the class from a color, a memory of a table, or another hall. No edition, no class, whatever word the slide used.

---

## 1. First-Principles Engineering Formulation and Governing Mathematics

In high-density data center environments, verbal summaries and qualitative status tiles routinely obscure incipient physical failures. Whether auditing a $120\,\text{kW}$ liquid-cooled rack boundary, evaluating a 1-second telemetry time series, or verifying plant redundancy prior to handover, the governing physical relationship for this protocol is expressed as:

$$d_{\text{Cu}} < 300\,\text{\AA}/30\text{d} \;\land\; d_{\text{Ag}} < 200\,\text{\AA}/30\text{d} \implies \text{ANSI/ISA-71.04-2013 Class G1}$$

When any term on the left-hand or right-hand side of this relationship is left unmeasured, inferred from an uncalibrated nameplate, or averaged across an unverified time window, the resulting engineering record cannot support a valid operational signature. Field engineers must verify each physical variable independently using NIST/ISO 17025 traceable instruments before proceeding to the next gate in the sequence.

| Audit Verification Parameter | Unacceptable / Defective Field Practice | Auditable First-Principles Requirement | Mandatory Action on Failure |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Primary Boundary Definition** | Implied by vendor brochure or slide deck | Explicitly bounded on stamped P&ID / SLD with tag IDs | Halt acceptance; issue formal boundary clarification |
| **Measurement & Telemetry Proof** | Single uncalibrated display reading or 60-sec average | Calibrated Class A/0.5S sensor with 1-sec UTC timestamp | Reject dataset; classify point as `0x40` Stale or `0x80` Bad |
| **Pass / Fail Acceptance Gate** | Qualitative "Looks OK" or "Within Normal Range" | Quantitative numerical corridor cited from revision in force | Log Category A/B defect; withhold retainage or permit |
| **Custody & Sign-Off Record** | Single bundled "Accepted" signature at end of meeting | Scoped, dated sentence naming exact proved & unproved lines | Strike unsupported claims; issue Conditional Refusal |

---

## 2. Deep-Dive Technical Protocol and Field Implementation

The following field protocol—adapted directly from **Volume 08: *Judge a Corrosion Coupon***—establishes the step-by-step verification mechanics required on the data hall floor:

You are judging whether gases in the air are consuming metal on the equipment, fast enough that you are not willing to call the room fit for the boards you intend to run. You are not judging cleanliness in the housekeeping sense. A room can be swept and still be corrosive. A room can look hazy and not be the problem this sheet is for.

The metal that matters changed when boards stopped using the old leaded finish. Immersion silver, and solders of tin, copper, and silver, put silver where the joint is. Silver is not a decoration. It is a path. Gases that attack silver can open a joint while the copper in the same room still looks acceptable. A pass on copper alone is not a pass. Write both metals, or write that you did not measure silver and you will not claim the joints.

This is not the corrosion of a steel pipe in a water loop. Iron in a chilled-water report does not tell you about the air at a board. Do not staple those reports together and call them one trend. Different metal, different path, different sheet.

Smell is not a measurement. A nose adapts, and many of the gases that matter do not announce themselves at the concentration that hurts a joint. A particle counter is not a measurement of this problem either. Particles and gases travel together often enough that people mix the sentences. A filter that catches dust has not necessarily caught the gas. If the only instrument in the pack is a particle counter, you do not have a corrosion result. You have a dust result. File it on a different line.

## What this is not

A shorted board has many causes. Dust, moisture, a bad joint from the day it was made, a scratch, a cleaner someone sprayed. Gas corrosion is one cause, and only after the coupon says the air could do it. Do not use this sheet to close a failure investigation. The coupon does not identify which joint failed, and it does not date the failure. If a board failed in the interval, write that as a separate fact, with its own owner. Mixing them is how a bad hang becomes a vendor's fault, or a real air problem becomes a manufacturing story. Leave both open until each has its own evidence.

Do not import a water-treatment trend, a particle count, or a temperature map to fill a missing silver strip. Adjacent measurements are conditions or other problems. They are not a substitute metal. If the only reason you believe the air is fit is that the room is cool and the floor is clean, you believe a different sheet. Say so. Do not sign this one.

## What a result is allowed to mean



A coupon result supports one sentence: over this interval, at this place, this metal reacted at the rate the report states, and the report's method names a class or it does not. It does not support "the hall is safe," "the city is dirty," or "the boards will fail by a date." Failure dates are not in the coupon. If someone offers one, label it a guess. Guesses do not go in the sentence.

A class name without the report's method is a word. You may not carry it onto a slide as if you had measured it. Cite the standard's title and edition when the report cites them. Do not reconstruct the class from memory of a table. If you do not have the report, you do not have the class.

## Electrochemical Creep Corrosion on Immersion Silver (ImAg) and SAC305 Solder

### Why Copper Coupons Alone Fail to Detect Reduced-Sulfur Attack on Silver

Under **ANSI/ISA-71.04-2013** (*Environmental Conditions for Process Measurement and Control Systems: Airborne Contaminants*) and **ASHRAE TC 9.9** guidance for RoHS-compliant lead-free IT equipment (which utilizes immersion silver PCB finishes and tin-silver-copper SAC305 solder joints), whitespace air quality is governed by the quantitative corrosion film growth rate on **both** copper ($\text{Cu}$) and silver ($\text{Ag}$) reference strips normalized to a 30-day exposure window:

$$2\text{Ag} + \text{H}_2\text{S} + \frac{1}{2}\text{O}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{RH}} \text{Ag}_2\text{S} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

Because reduced sulfur species ($\text{H}_2\text{S}$, carbonyl sulfide $\text{OCS}$, elemental sulfur $\text{S}_8$) combined with oxidizing gases ($\text{NO}_2, \text{O}_3, \text{Cl}_2$) and relative humidity ($\text{RH} > 50\%$) drive aggressive silver sulfide ($\text{Ag}_2\text{S}$) whisker creep across fine-pitch PCB traces even when copper reactivity remains below $300\,\text{\AA}/30\text{d}$, environmental acceptance requires dual-metal verification paired with strict chain-of-custody controls.

# Where you hang the coupon is the sentence

> **Direct Answer Block**: Where to hang copper and silver corrosion coupons in a data center—outdoor makeup, post-filter plenum, cold aisle intake, and hot return—and what each location proves. In mission-critical data center commissioning and operations, engineers enforce this boundary using deterministic physical equations, calibrated field instrumentation, and auditable sign-off gates rather than relying on vendor brochure summaries, uncalibrated software plots, or verbal assurances. Every measurement and state transition must be recorded with synchronized UTC timestamps and explicit pass/fail thresholds before a signature is granted.

![Discharge does not prove the room.](figures/flagship/fig-03-data-hall-coupon-placement-topology.png)

A coupon measures the air that touched it. It does not measure the hall. A strip in the return, a strip in the supply, and a strip at the board face are three sentences. A meeting will try to merge them. Do not sign the merge.

If the claim is that the boards are in fit air, hang the strip where the boards live. A strip in the treatment unit's discharge proves the unit can clean air it just cleaned. It does not prove the room. That is the same trick as calling a probe in a stub an inlet.

You want a strip on the source as well, makeup before treatment, if you are about to buy a machine. Without it, a bad room result does not tell you whether the outdoors or a hole is the driver. Without the room strip, a bad outdoor result does not tell you whether the building already keeps it out.

A short visit is not a year. Outdoor air and humidity change with the season. Indoor treatment can look fine until makeup volume rises. If the loud season is missing, refuse the annual sentence. Write the weeks you actually hung. This article will not invent a minimum number of days.

## 1. First-Principles Engineering Formulation and Governing Mathematics

In high-density data center environments, verbal summaries and qualitative status tiles routinely obscure incipient physical failures. Whether auditing a $120\,\text{kW}$ liquid-cooled rack boundary, evaluating a 1-second telemetry time series, or verifying plant redundancy prior to handover, the governing physical relationship for this protocol is expressed as:

$$d_{\text{film}} = \frac{I_{\text{red}} \cdot t_{\text{red}} \cdot M_{\text{mol}}}{n \cdot F \cdot A_{\text{surface}} \cdot \rho_{\text{film}}} \times 10^8\,\text{\AA}$$

When any term on the left-hand or right-hand side of this relationship is left unmeasured, inferred from an uncalibrated nameplate, or averaged across an unverified time window, the resulting engineering record cannot support a valid operational signature. ## 2. Deep-Dive Technical Protocol and Field Implementation

The following field protocol—adapted directly from **Volume 08: *Judge a Corrosion Coupon***—establishes the step-by-step verification mechanics required on the data hall floor:

The coupon measures the air that touched it. It does not measure the hall. A strip in the return says what left the room. A strip in the supply says what the unit delivered. A strip at the face of a board says what that board saw. These are three sentences. A meeting will try to make them one. Do not sign the merged sentence.

Hang the one that matches the claim. If the claim is that the boards are in fit air, the coupon belongs where the boards live, not in the prettiest aisle and not inside the treatment unit's own discharge. A coupon in the discharge proves the unit can clean the air it just cleaned. It does not prove the room. That trick is the same shape as a temperature probe in a supply stub being called an inlet. The fourth book already refused the stub. Refuse the discharge.

Height and facing matter enough to write down. A strip on top of a cabinet in a dead pocket is a different sample from a strip in the stream that feeds the face. You do not need a model to know they differ. You need to write which one you hung, so the next person does not hang the other and announce a trend. If you cannot describe the place without a room number that identifies a site, describe the function: board face, cold aisle, supply leaving the unit, return entering the unit, makeup before treatment, makeup after treatment. Function is enough. The site name stays in their file.

## Outside and inside

A coupon outside, or in the makeup before any treatment, is the source. A coupon inside is the result after the building has done whatever it does. You want both if you are about to spend money on treatment. Without the outside coupon, a bad inside result does not tell you whether the city, the street, a loading dock, or a dead animal in a duct is the source. You will buy the wrong machine. Without the inside coupon, a bad outside result does not tell you whether the building already keeps it out. You will buy a machine for a problem the envelope already solved.

Do not hang one coupon "for the site" and let every room inherit it. A sealed electrical room and a hall with a propped door are not the same air. One coupon per sentence. If you cannot afford two, write which sentence you are not supporting. Absence is allowed. Inheritance is not.

## People move them

A coupon that was taken down for a tour, then rehung, has a gap. Write the gap. Do not let the lab's single rate cover the days it was in a drawer. A coupon moved from the board face to the return halfway, without a note, is two places and no result. Treat it as missing. Chapter 6 of the monitor book: missing is not zero, and it is not a pass.

## 3. Field Verification Checklist and Instrumentation Hygiene

To execute this protocol without introducing measurement bias or scope ambiguity, the responsible engineer enforces four mandatory field rules:
1. **Instrument Traceability Before Observation**: Verify that every thermometer (4-wire Pt100 RTD Class A), pressure transducer ($\le \pm 0.1\%$ span), flowmeter, balometer, or power analyzer carries a current calibration certificate and passes a pre-test zero/span check on the day of the walk.
2. **Synchronized Time-Series Capture**: Align all digital loggers and gateway pollers to a single UTC reference clock (via IEEE 1588v2 PTP at $\pm 1\,\text{ms}$ for electrical Sequence of Events, or NTP at $\pm 10\,\text{ms}$ for thermal/hydraulic dwells). Never merge unsynchronized CSV files by row index.
3. **Explicit Isolation of Disturbances vs. Control Handles**: Hold upstream supply temperatures, parallel cabinet loads, and containment door states constant during the observation dwell so that transient plant drift is never mistaken for steady-state equipment performance.
4. **Written Record Prior to Signature**: Record every boundary tag, measured value, uncertainty tolerance, and open limitation in ink on the controlled project sheet before leaving the equipment line-up.

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

### Why does "Where you hang the coupon is the sentence" matter during high-density data center commissioning and operations?
Where to hang copper and silver corrosion coupons in a data center—outdoor makeup, post-filter plenum, cold aisle intake, and hot return—and what each location proves. When project teams bypass this rule to meet a commercial schedule milestone, unverified physical assumptions—such as hidden hydraulic pressure drops, unlogged polling gaps, unblanked bypass leakage, or uncalibrated sensor offsets—transfer directly into live 24/7 production as latent single points of failure.

### How do you quantitatively verify compliance with "corrosion coupon placement data hall supply return" on the physical floor?
Compliance is verified by executing the governing mathematical balance ($$d_{\text{film}} = \frac{I_{\text{red}} \cdot t_{\text{red}} \cdot M_{\text{mol}}}{n \cdot F \cdot A_{\text{surface}} \cdot \rho_{\text{film}}} \times 10^8\,\text{\AA}$$) using independent, calibrated field instruments across a stabilized steady-state dwell window (minimum 15 to 30 minutes for thermal and hydraulic systems), and confirming that the discrepancy between primary and secondary measurements remains strictly within the pre-declared acceptance band.

### What should an engineer do if a contractor or vendor submits a report that violates this protocol?
The reviewing engineer must refuse to sign the broad acceptance sentence, mark the specific line item as **Unproved / Defective** on the official audit sheet, and either require a witnessed re-test under a corrected script or isolate the unproved scope under a time-bounded Conditional Acceptance with a $150\%$ to $200\%$ financial retainage escrow holdback.

# Seal the room before you buy the cleaner

> **Direct Answer Block**: Why sealing data hall cable penetrations, airlocks, and vapor barriers to maintain >= +12.5 Pa positive pressurization must precede purchasing recirculation scrubbers. In mission-critical data center commissioning and operations, engineers enforce this boundary using deterministic physical equations, calibrated field instrumentation, and auditable sign-off gates rather than relying on vendor brochure summaries, uncalibrated software plots, or verbal assurances. Every measurement and state transition must be recorded with synchronized UTC timestamps and explicit pass/fail thresholds before a signature is granted.

![Seal, then treat makeup, then hang the after.](figures/flagship/fig-04-chemical-filtration-media-and-breakthrough.png)

A treatment unit in a room that leaks is cleaning air that is already leaving, while outdoor air enters through paths nobody listed. Cable trays, wall penetrations, a door that does not latch, a relief path with no name: each hole breaks the sentence "the unit holds the room."

Close the holes you can see, and date the closing against the coupon interval. An interval that straddles the sealing mixes before and after into one rate. Pull the strip or hang another. Do not seal a life-safety path because it was convenient. That path stays open on purpose, and it is a source. Treat the air that uses it, or accept that this path is untreated.

Then look at makeup. Indoor treatment loses when untreated outdoor air arrives in more volume than the room unit can take. A coupon only in the room, while makeup is untreated, supports a weaker sentence: this rate, while dirty air was still allowed in. Do not upgrade it because one month improved.

Start the after coupon when air is going through the intake treatment, not when the purchase order is signed. One strip across both dates lets a late install borrow the credit of an early seal.

---

## 1. First-Principles Engineering Formulation and Governing Mathematics

In high-density data center environments, verbal summaries and qualitative status tiles routinely obscure incipient physical failures. Whether auditing a $120\,\text{kW}$ liquid-cooled rack boundary, evaluating a 1-second telemetry time series, or verifying plant redundancy prior to handover, the governing physical relationship for this protocol is expressed as:

$$\Delta P_{\text{hall}} = \frac{\rho_{\text{air}}}{2}\left(\frac{Q_{\text{makeup}} - Q_{\text{exhaust}}}{C_d \cdot A_{\text{leak}}}\right)^2 \ge +12.5\,\text{Pa}$$

When any term on the left-hand or right-hand side of this relationship is left unmeasured, inferred from an uncalibrated nameplate, or averaged across an unverified time window, the resulting engineering record cannot support a valid operational signature. Field engineers must verify each physical variable independently using NIST/ISO 17025 traceable instruments before proceeding to the next gate in the sequence.

| Audit Verification Parameter | Unacceptable / Defective Field Practice | Auditable First-Principles Requirement | Mandatory Action on Failure |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Primary Boundary Definition** | Implied by vendor brochure or slide deck | Explicitly bounded on stamped P&ID / SLD with tag IDs | Halt acceptance; issue formal boundary clarification |
| **Measurement & Telemetry Proof** | Single uncalibrated display reading or 60-sec average | Calibrated Class A/0.5S sensor with 1-sec UTC timestamp | Reject dataset; classify point as `0x40` Stale or `0x80` Bad |
| **Pass / Fail Acceptance Gate** | Qualitative "Looks OK" or "Within Normal Range" | Quantitative numerical corridor cited from revision in force | Log Category A/B defect; withhold retainage or permit |
| **Custody & Sign-Off Record** | Single bundled "Accepted" signature at end of meeting | Scoped, dated sentence naming exact proved & unproved lines | Strike unsupported claims; issue Conditional Refusal |

---

## 2. Deep-Dive Technical Protocol and Field Implementation

The following field protocol—adapted directly from **Volume 08: *Judge a Corrosion Coupon***—establishes the step-by-step verification mechanics required on the data hall floor:

The first work is the envelope, not the catalog. A treatment unit in a room that leaks is cleaning air that is already leaving, and outdoor air that is already entering, through paths nobody listed. Cable trays, wall penetrations, unsealed floors, a door that does not latch, a relief path with no control: each is a hole in the sentence "the unit holds the room." Close the holes you can see, then hang the coupon. Do not hang it, buy the unit, and seal later. Later's coupon will not tell you which action did the work.

Write what you closed, by function, not by a photograph album of a named hall. A photograph can be evidence in their file that a penetration was sealed. It is not the sheet. The sheet says which class of hole you closed, the date, and whether the coupon interval was before or after. An interval that straddles the sealing is the same defect as an interval that straddles the treatment. Chapter 2. Pull it or hang another.

## Where to look, by function

Look at paths a cable uses: trays that leave the room, cutouts under a raised floor, sleeves that were sealed once and then pulled through again. Look at doors that do not latch, at relief that was blocked with a board, at the joint between a unit and the opening it sits in. Look at the makeup intake before you look at the catalog. You are not performing a tightness test this piece does not own. You are listing holes by function so the coupon interval knows what was open. A number from a blower-door test, if they have one, stays in their report. It does not replace the list. A tight number with a propped door during the hang is a tight number about a different week.

Write the list before the coupon goes up, and again when you take it down. The second list is how you notice the cable pull. One list, made from memory after a bad report, is a story. Stories do not choose the next machine.

## What sealing is not

Sealing is not a promise that the room is a laboratory. Doors will open. People will enter. The claim is that uncontrolled paths are closed, and the paths that remain are the ones you meant: a door that shuts, a makeup path you can point to, a relief path you can point to. If you cannot point to the intended path, the room is still leaking through a path you have not found. Look again before you buy. A unit sized for a leak you have not found will be the wrong size, and this piece will not give you the size. Sizing is their calculation, in their file, from a method they can show. It is not a number you invent in the corridor.

Do not seal a relief or a smoke path because it was convenient to the corrosion sentence. Life safety paper wins. If a path must stay open for that paper, it is an intended path. Treat the air that uses it, or accept that this path is a source. Do not hide the path in the sealing note as "closed."

## Recheck

Seals fail. A cable pull next month opens what you closed. The coupon does not know why the rate returned. The note has to. If work opened the envelope during an interval, that interval is tainted the same way a moved coupon is tainted. Mark it. Do not let a vendor call the return a proof that you need a larger machine. You may need a larger machine. You may need the hole closed again. The coupon alone cannot say which. Go and look.

## Building Envelope Vapor Barriers and Positive Pressurization Hydraulics

### Calculating Makeup Air Volume Required to Prevent Unfiltered Infiltration

Under **ANSI/ISA-71.04-2013** (*Environmental Conditions for Process Measurement and Control Systems: Airborne Contaminants*) and **ASHRAE TC 9.9** guidance for RoHS-compliant lead-free IT equipment (which utilizes immersion silver PCB finishes and tin-silver-copper SAC305 solder joints), whitespace air quality is governed by the quantitative corrosion film growth rate on **both** copper ($\text{Cu}$) and silver ($\text{Ag}$) reference strips normalized to a 30-day exposure window:

$$\Delta P_{\text{hall}} = \frac{\rho_{\text{air}}}{2} \left( \frac{Q_{\text{makeup}} - Q_{\text{exhaust}}}{C_d \cdot A_{\text{envelope\_leak}}} \right)^2 \ge +12.5\,\text{Pa}$$

Because reduced sulfur species ($\text{H}_2\text{S}$, carbonyl sulfide $\text{OCS}$, elemental sulfur $\text{S}_8$) combined with oxidizing gases ($\text{NO}_2, \text{O}_3, \text{Cl}_2$) and relative humidity ($\text{RH} > 50\%$) drive aggressive silver sulfide ($\text{Ag}_2\text{S}$) whisker creep across fine-pitch PCB traces even when copper reactivity remains below $300\,\text{\AA}/30\text{d}$, environmental acceptance requires dual-metal verification paired with strict chain-of-custody controls.

| Corrosion Audit Parameter | Unacceptable / Defective Practice | First-Principles Engineering Requirement (ISA-71.04 / ASTM B825) | Mandatory Refusal or Remediation Action |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Core Chapter Focus** | Sealing Cable Penetrations, Airlocks, and Battery Room Exhausts Before Buying Media | Dual $\text{Cu} + \text{Ag}$ coulometric reduction with documented exposure timestamps | Refuse any environmental fitness claim missing $\text{Ag}$ or hang interval |
| **Class G1 Mild Pass Gate** | Quoting Copper rate alone ($<300\,\text{\AA}$) or visual strip color | $d_{\text{Cu}} < 300\,\text{\AA}/30\text{d}$ **AND** $d_{\text{Ag}} < 200\,\text{\AA}/30\text{d}$ (zero $\text{Cu}_2\text{S}$ on copper) | Classify G2 ($<1000/1000\,\text{\AA}$), G3 ($<2000/2000\,\text{\AA}$), or GX as non-compliant |
| **Chain of Custody & Blank** | Mailing strips without a sealed Field Travel Blank (`FTB`) | Sealed lot-matched travel blank $d_{\text{blank}} \le 25\text{--}35\,\text{\AA}$ subtracted/verified | Invalidate "Fit" certification if no unopened travel blank accompanied lot |
| **Filtration & Envelope Proof** | Installing recirculation filters in an unsealed negative-$\Delta P$ hall | Vapor-sealed envelope ($\Delta P \ge +12.5\,\text{Pa}$) + gas-matched media ($\text{EBCT} \ge 0.2\,\text{s}$) | Pull coupon at any media/envelope change; start new post-change interval |

# What a corrosion coupon report must show

> **Direct Answer Block**: Forensic checklist for auditing laboratory corrosion coupon reports: coulometric stripping plateaus, Cu2S/Ag2S speciation, actual hang intervals, and travel blanks. In mission-critical data center commissioning and operations, engineers enforce this boundary using deterministic physical equations, calibrated field instrumentation, and auditable sign-off gates rather than relying on vendor brochure summaries, uncalibrated software plots, or verbal assurances. Every measurement and state transition must be recorded with synchronized UTC timestamps and explicit pass/fail thresholds before a signature is granted.

![Two metals, a clock, an edition, or no class.](figures/flagship/fig-05-makeup-air-pressurization-and-leak-paths.png)

A slide that says the room is G1 is not a report. The report is the record. If you cannot get it, you cannot sign the class.

It names the metal, not "coupon." Copper and silver are separate lines. A single collapsed index does not clear the joints. It names the method well enough that another lab would know what was asked, without you pasting their procedure. It names the place by function: board face, supply, return, makeup before treatment, makeup after, or the unit discharge. Discharge does not support the room. It names the start and the end. A rate with no hang time is a normalized month hiding a short visit. Do not use it. The rate keeps the unit the lab printed. Do not convert it in the meeting to match a table you remember.

If a class is printed, the edition is printed beside it. No edition, no class. "Equivalent to" a class is a translation. Strike it unless the translation rule is written. This note does not rebuild that table, and it does not supply the missing edition from memory.

A blank from the same lot, unopened to the room air, belongs in the same file. No blank, no fit class. The trip and the lab have to be bounded, or "fit" may be the mailer.

Who read the metal signs the report. If the reader is the seller, the read is a hypothesis until a second method agrees. Agreement is the same metal, place, and interval. A nod in the meeting is not a second read.

## 1. First-Principles Engineering Formulation and Governing Mathematics

In high-density data center environments, verbal summaries and qualitative status tiles routinely obscure incipient physical failures. Whether auditing a $120\,\text{kW}$ liquid-cooled rack boundary, evaluating a 1-second telemetry time series, or verifying plant redundancy prior to handover, the governing physical relationship for this protocol is expressed as:

$$d_{\text{norm}}(30\text{d}) = \left(d_{\text{exposed}} - d_{\text{blank}}\right) \cdot \left(\frac{30}{t_{\text{hang\_days}}}\right)^n$$

When any term on the left-hand or right-hand side of this relationship is left unmeasured, inferred from an uncalibrated nameplate, or averaged across an unverified time window, the resulting engineering record cannot support a valid operational signature. Field engineers must verify each physical variable independently using NIST/ISO 17025 traceable instruments before proceeding to the next gate in the sequence.

## 2. Deep-Dive Technical Protocol and Field Implementation

The following field protocol—adapted directly from **Volume 08: *Judge a Corrosion Coupon***—establishes the step-by-step verification mechanics required on the data hall floor:

The report is the record. The slide is not. Read the report before the meeting in which someone wants the class in a sentence. If you cannot get the report, you cannot sign the class. A verbal "we are G1" is the kinder summary. Chapter 8 of the handover book refused those. This one too.

## What has to be on it

The metal, named, not "coupon." The method the lab used, named well enough that a second lab would know what was asked, without you pasting their procedure into this piece. The place, by function, matching the sheet. The start and the end. The rate, with its unit, and the hang time visible so you are not asked to trust a normalized month that hides a short visit. Chapter 2.

If a class is printed, the edition is printed next to it. No edition, no class, whatever word they used. "Equivalent to" a class is not the class. It is a translation someone made. Ask for the translation rule in writing, or strike the word. You will not reconstruct the rule in the margin.

A statement of what the method does not cover is part of a usable report. If it is missing, you do not invent the caveat. You write "coverage not stated" on the sheet and you do not let the class travel further than the metal and the interval. Coverage not stated is a limit. It is not a pass.

## What you strike

A photograph of the strip as the result. A rate with no unit. A rate whose interval is the day the courier delivered the mailer. A class applied to "the data hall" when the place line says return, or discharge, or a room that is not the one with the boards. A combined copper-and-silver index you cannot split. A comparison to another site, with that site's name showing. Strike the comparison and do not copy the name into your note. Their identifier stays in their file.

A report that arrived after you already told a customer the class is a late point. Chapter 3 of the monitor book. It may correct the record. It does not silently rewrite the notice. If the late number would have changed what you said, write a new sentence. Do not edit the old one into a smoother class.

## Units

Leave the rate in the unit the report used. Do not convert it in the meeting to match a table you remember, and do not convert it twice, once in the note and once on the slide. A conversion you cannot show in one line is a new number. New numbers are tests you did not run. If two reports use two units, ask the lab, or refuse the comparison. Do not average them into a monthly figure so the chart lines up. The clock chapter already refused averaged clocks. Averaged rates are the same defect.

A class does not have a unit. It is a word the report is allowed to print only beside an edition. If someone prints the class and not the rate, ask for the rate. A class without a rate is a headline. Headlines do not go on the sheet as the result. The rate stays in their pdf. Your sheet says the rate is filed, and where. You do not need the digits in your handwriting for the refusal to be real. You need them in the report if you are going to sign the class.

## Who signed the pdf

The person who read the metal signs the report, by name or by the lab's role, not by the vendor's sales deck. If the reader and the seller are the same party, chapter 2 already marked it a hypothesis until a second read agrees. Agreement is the same metal, place, and interval. A second vendor who says "looks right" is not a second read.

Chain of custody is a sentence, not a form you must reprint. Who took it down, who carried it, whether it sat in a hot vehicle or an open drawer. If nobody can say, the interval includes unknown hours. Unknown hours are a gap. A gap does not support a fine class. You may still file the report. You may not call it clean custody.

# Why a corrosion test needs a blank coupon

> **Direct Answer Block**: Why every batch of exposed data center corrosion coupons must travel with an unopened, lot-matched Field Travel Blank (FTB) to isolate transit and lab background noise. In mission-critical data center commissioning and operations, engineers enforce this boundary using deterministic physical equations, calibrated field instrumentation, and auditable sign-off gates rather than relying on vendor brochure summaries, uncalibrated software plots, or verbal assurances. Every measurement and state transition must be recorded with synchronized UTC timestamps and explicit pass/fail thresholds before a signature is granted.

![The blank bounds the trip.](figures/flagship/fig-06-passive-coupons-vs-realtime-qcm-monitors.png)

The strip that hung in the room is the sample. The strip that traveled in a sealed bag and never saw that air is the blank. It tells you what the mailer, the vehicle, and the lab did to the metal. Without it, a bad rate might be the journey. You will treat a room for a courier. A fine rate might be the bag. You will sign fit for a trip.

Send a blank from the same lot, same metal, same mailer. If the lab will not report it apart from the sample, you do not know what fraction of the rate is the room. Do not assign the whole rate to the boards. Do not open the blank to show a visitor a clean strip. An opened blank is spoiled. A spoiled blank does not clear the trip.

The blank does not replace a room coupon, and a clean blank does not average away a bad board-face strip. It only bounds the trip. If the blank moved as much as the sample, the place sentence is refused until the trip is understood. That refusal does not require the digits reprinted here. It requires the comparison the report already printed, read honestly.

No blank is allowed only if you are not signing a fit class. A harsh result can still be a reason to look. Fit without a blank is fit you cannot separate from the mailer. Do not write "subject to blank later." Later does not reconstruct a bag you did not send. File the blank's report next to the sample's. A blank filed somewhere else will be forgotten the day someone wants the word fit.

---

## 1. First-Principles Engineering Formulation and Governing Mathematics

In high-density data center environments, verbal summaries and qualitative status tiles routinely obscure incipient physical failures. Whether auditing a $120\,\text{kW}$ liquid-cooled rack boundary, evaluating a 1-second telemetry time series, or verifying plant redundancy prior to handover, the governing physical relationship for this protocol is expressed as:

$$d_{\text{blank, Cu}} \le 35\,\text{\AA} \;\land\; d_{\text{blank, Ag}} \le 25\,\text{\AA} \implies \text{Valid Chain of Custody}$$

When any term on the left-hand or right-hand side of this relationship is left unmeasured, inferred from an uncalibrated nameplate, or averaged across an unverified time window, the resulting engineering record cannot support a valid operational signature. Field engineers must verify each physical variable independently using NIST/ISO 17025 traceable instruments before proceeding to the next gate in the sequence.

| Audit Verification Parameter | Unacceptable / Defective Field Practice | Auditable First-Principles Requirement | Mandatory Action on Failure |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Primary Boundary Definition** | Implied by vendor brochure or slide deck | Explicitly bounded on stamped P&ID / SLD with tag IDs | Halt acceptance; issue formal boundary clarification |
| **Measurement & Telemetry Proof** | Single uncalibrated display reading or 60-sec average | Calibrated Class A/0.5S sensor with 1-sec UTC timestamp | Reject dataset; classify point as `0x40` Stale or `0x80` Bad |
| **Pass / Fail Acceptance Gate** | Qualitative "Looks OK" or "Within Normal Range" | Quantitative numerical corridor cited from revision in force | Log Category A/B defect; withhold retainage or permit |
| **Custody & Sign-Off Record** | Single bundled "Accepted" signature at end of meeting | Scoped, dated sentence naming exact proved & unproved lines | Strike unsupported claims; issue Conditional Refusal |

## 2. Deep-Dive Technical Protocol and Field Implementation

The following field protocol—adapted directly from **Volume 08: *Judge a Corrosion Coupon***—establishes the step-by-step verification mechanics required on the data hall floor:

A coupon that traveled in a sealed bag, and was never hung, is a blank. It tells you what the mailer, the vehicle, and the lab did to the metal before anyone calls the result the room. Without it, a bad rate might be the journey. You will then treat a room for a courier. Hang the real strips. Send a blank from the same lot, same metal, same mailer, unopened to the air you care about. If the lab cannot tell a blank from a sample in the report, ask them to. If they will not, you do not know what fraction of the rate is the trip. Do not assign the whole rate to the boards.

The blank is not a second room. It does not clear a bad board-face strip by being cleaner, and it does not condemn the room by being dirty. It bounds the trip. Write both rates as filed, in their report, not in this piece. If the blank moved as much as the sample, the sample's place sentence is refused until you understand the trip. That refusal does not need their number reprinted. It needs the comparison they already printed, read honestly.

## The lot

Strips from different lots are not a pair, even if both say silver. A lot that was already tarnished in the tin is a tainted zero. Ask whether the lab or the vendor records the lot. If nobody does, say so. You can still hang them. You cannot call a small difference between two hangs a trend. Trend needs the same lot, or an explicit statement that lot does not matter, from the method, not from hope.

Do not touch the face you intend them to read. Skin, cleaner, and a glove that is not the one their method names are a treatment you did not record. If their method is silent, silence is not permission. Handle by the edge, or do not handle. This is not a procedure for preparing metal. It is a refusal to become an unrecorded source.

## Opening the bag

Open the sample bag at the place, at the start time you will write, not in the office the day before. An hour on a desk is an hour in the wrong air, and it will be averaged into the room. If you must stage them, keep them sealed and write the staging. Sealed and forgotten in a hot cabinet is still a condition. Note it, or do not use the rate for a fine class.

Take them down into a bag at the end time, at the place. A strip carried open across the hall, then across a loading dock, has a second exposure. That second exposure is usually shorter than the hang. It is still unaudited. Bag at the place. The blank never leaves its bag. If someone opened the blank "just to check," it is not a blank. Mark it spoiled. Do not average it into a story that the trip was clean.

## What the lab owes the blank

The report names the blank's metal and that it was not exposed by you, or it does not mention a blank. No mention: write "no blank" on the sheet. No blank is allowed only if you are not signing a fine class. A coarse, obvious attack may still be discussed as a hypothesis. A class that means "fit" requires the trip to have been bounded. Otherwise fit may be the bag, or the attack may be the bag. You cannot tell. Not telling is a refusal, not a delay. Do not write "subject to blank later." Later does not reconstruct a bag you did not send.

Keep the blank's report in the same file as the sample's report. A blank filed somewhere else will be forgotten the day someone wants a fit sentence. Forgotten blank, no fit class. That is the whole rule, applied at filing time rather than in the meeting.

## Statistical Quality Control Using Field Travel Blanks (FTB) and Lot Controls

### Detecting Transit Contamination, Mailer Outgassing, and Lab Stripping Offset

Under **ANSI/ISA-71.04-2013** (*Environmental Conditions for Process Measurement and Control Systems: Airborne Contaminants*) and **ASHRAE TC 9.9** guidance for RoHS-compliant lead-free IT equipment (which utilizes immersion silver PCB finishes and tin-silver-copper SAC305 solder joints), whitespace air quality is governed by the quantitative corrosion film growth rate on **both** copper ($\text{Cu}$) and silver ($\text{Ag}$) reference strips normalized to a 30-day exposure window:

$$d_{\text{blank}} \le 35\,\text{\AA} \text{ (Cu)} \;\land\; d_{\text{blank}} \le 25\,\text{\AA} \text{ (Ag)} \implies \text{Valid Chain of Custody}$$

Because reduced sulfur species ($\text{H}_2\text{S}$, carbonyl sulfide $\text{OCS}$, elemental sulfur $\text{S}_8$) combined with oxidizing gases ($\text{NO}_2, \text{O}_3, \text{Cl}_2$) and relative humidity ($\text{RH} > 50\%$) drive aggressive silver sulfide ($\text{Ag}_2\text{S}$) whisker creep across fine-pitch PCB traces even when copper reactivity remains below $300\,\text{\AA}/30\text{d}$, environmental acceptance requires dual-metal verification paired with strict chain-of-custody controls.

| Corrosion Audit Parameter | Unacceptable / Defective Practice | First-Principles Engineering Requirement (ISA-71.04 / ASTM B825) | Mandatory Refusal or Remediation Action |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Core Chapter Focus** | Invalidating Fit Classifications When Travel Blanks Exceed Baseline Noise | Dual $\text{Cu} + \text{Ag}$ coulometric reduction with documented exposure timestamps | Refuse any environmental fitness claim missing $\text{Ag}$ or hang interval |
| **Class G1 Mild Pass Gate** | Quoting Copper rate alone ($<300\,\text{\AA}$) or visual strip color | $d_{\text{Cu}} < 300\,\text{\AA}/30\text{d}$ **AND** $d_{\text{Ag}} < 200\,\text{\AA}/30\text{d}$ (zero $\text{Cu}_2\text{S}$ on copper) | Classify G2 ($<1000/1000\,\text{\AA}$), G3 ($<2000/2000\,\text{\AA}$), or GX as non-compliant |
| **Chain of Custody & Blank** | Mailing strips without a sealed Field Travel Blank (`FTB`) | Sealed lot-matched travel blank $d_{\text{blank}} \le 25\text{--}35\,\text{\AA}$ subtracted/verified | Invalidate "Fit" certification if no unopened travel blank accompanied lot |
| **Filtration & Envelope Proof** | Installing recirculation filters in an unsealed negative-$\Delta P$ hall | Vapor-sealed envelope ($\Delta P \ge +12.5\,\text{Pa}$) + gas-matched media ($\text{EBCT} \ge 0.2\,\text{s}$) | Pull coupon at any media/envelope change; start new post-change interval |

## 3. Field Verification Checklist and Instrumentation Hygiene

To execute this protocol without introducing measurement bias or scope ambiguity, the responsible engineer enforces four mandatory field rules:
1. **Instrument Traceability Before Observation**: Verify that every thermometer (4-wire Pt100 RTD Class A), pressure transducer ($\le \pm 0.1\%$ span), flowmeter, balometer, or power analyzer carries a current calibration certificate and passes a pre-test zero/span check on the day of the walk.
2. **Synchronized Time-Series Capture**: Align all digital loggers and gateway pollers to a single UTC reference clock (via IEEE 1588v2 PTP at $\pm 1\,\text{ms}$ for electrical Sequence of Events, or NTP at $\pm 10\,\text{ms}$ for thermal/hydraulic dwells). Never merge unsynchronized CSV files by row index.
3. **Explicit Isolation of Disturbances vs. Control Handles**: Hold upstream supply temperatures, parallel cabinet loads, and containment door states constant during the observation dwell so that transient plant drift is never mistaken for steady-state equipment performance.
4. **Written Record Prior to Signature**: Record every boundary tag, measured value, uncertainty tolerance, and open limitation in ink on the controlled project sheet before leaving the equipment line-up.

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

### Why does "Why a corrosion test needs a blank coupon" matter during high-density data center commissioning and operations?
Why every batch of exposed data center corrosion coupons must travel with an unopened, lot-matched Field Travel Blank (FTB) to isolate transit and lab background noise. When project teams bypass this rule to meet a commercial schedule milestone, unverified physical assumptions—such as hidden hydraulic pressure drops, unlogged polling gaps, unblanked bypass leakage, or uncalibrated sensor offsets—transfer directly into live 24/7 production as latent single points of failure.

### How do you quantitatively verify compliance with "field travel blank corrosion coupon quality control" on the physical floor?
Compliance is verified by executing the governing mathematical balance ($$d_{\text{blank, Cu}} \le 35\,\text{\AA} \;\land\; d_{\text{blank, Ag}} \le 25\,\text{\AA} \implies \text{Valid Chain of Custody}$$) using independent, calibrated field instruments across a stabilized steady-state dwell window (minimum 15 to 30 minutes for thermal and hydraulic systems), and confirming that the discrepancy between primary and secondary measurements remains strictly within the pre-declared acceptance band.

### What should an engineer do if a contractor or vendor submits a report that violates this protocol?
The reviewing engineer must refuse to sign the broad acceptance sentence, mark the specific line item as **Unproved / Defective** on the official audit sheet, and either require a witnessed re-test under a corrected script or isolate the unproved scope under a time-bounded Conditional Acceptance with a $150\%$ to $200\%$ financial retainage escrow holdback.

# Count, identify, sample, witness: First-Principles Data Center Engineering Protocol

> **Direct Answer Block**: The four physical acts of a data center Technical Due Diligence (TDD) site walk—Count, Identify, Sample, and Witness—governed by square-root statistical sampling. In mission-critical data center commissioning and operations, engineers enforce this boundary using deterministic physical equations, calibrated field instrumentation, and auditable sign-off gates rather than relying on vendor brochure summaries, uncalibrated software plots, or verbal assurances. Every measurement and state transition must be recorded with synchronized UTC timestamps and explicit pass/fail thresholds before a signature is granted.

![Four acts, four verbs](figures/flagship/fig-01-tdd-audit-framework-and-red-flags.png)

A short visit will not retest the hall. It can still do four things that are not a tour.

Count what is in scope against their list, or say you only inventoried what you could see. A count without their list is not a reconciliation. Do not publish the list. Their identifiers stay in their file. Your note says the totals agreed, or where they did not, by function.

Identify on a sample rule written before you arrive. Present, matching the record, or not. A rule invented in the aisle to match the time you had is not a rule. If you check fewer than you wrote, the sentence narrows. It does not stay "identity verified." A newer substitute is not what was bought, unless the contract allows it and a document names it.

Sample the running state the same way. A dark machine is not a pass because the row looked full. Write dark. Do not infer health from a front panel. A dashboard of jobs is not a count of what was bought, and it is not an audit of the tenant's system.

Witness means you saw their test, or you saw the document that says it passed, and you say which. Their pass document is not your test. A demonstration staged for you, outside their script, is not a test either. If the document's scope is narrower than its title, use the scope. Titles lose.

In high-density data center environments, verbal summaries and qualitative status tiles routinely obscure incipient physical failures. Whether auditing a $120\,\text{kW}$ liquid-cooled rack boundary, evaluating a 1-second telemetry time series, or verifying plant redundancy prior to handover, the governing physical relationship for this protocol is expressed as:

$$n_{\text{sample}} = \lceil \sqrt{N_{\text{population}}} \rceil + 1, \qquad \varepsilon_{\text{mismatch}} = 0\%$$

When any term on the left-hand or right-hand side of this relationship is left unmeasured, inferred from an uncalibrated nameplate, or averaged across an unverified time window, the resulting engineering record cannot support a valid operational signature. ## 2. Deep-Dive Technical Protocol and Field Implementation

The following field protocol—adapted directly from **Volume 09: *Walk a TDD: Technical Due Diligence Physical Site Audit***—establishes the step-by-step verification mechanics required on the data hall floor:

On a short delivery you will not retest the hall. You can still do four things that are not a tour. Count. Identify. Sample. Witness.

Count is everything in scope, against their list, or a statement that the list was not there and you counted what you could see. A count without their list is an inventory, not a reconciliation. Say which. Do not publish the list. Their identifiers stay in their file. Your note says the totals agreed, or where they did not, by function.

Identify is a sample of identity, written before you arrive. How many, from which rows, compared to the asset record: present, matching, or not. A rule invented in the aisle to match what you had time for is not a rule. If you check fewer than you wrote, the sentence narrows. It does not stay "identity verified."

Sample the running state the same way. One or two machines in a row, configuration against the record, and whether it was actually running. A dark machine is not a pass because the row looked full. Write dark. Do not infer health from a front panel.

Witness means you saw their test, or you saw the document that says it passed, and you say which. Their pass document is not your test. The verification book already split those verbs. Use them. If you did not see the test, you do not write that you verified performance. You write that a document exists, who signed it, and that you did not rerun it.

Photographs are evidence in their file if the engagement allows them. They are not the finding. A photo of a nameplate is not a load. A photo of a screen is not a quality mark.

## What you write the same day

Write the four acts before you sleep, in the sheet, not in a chat. Count result. Sample as written or narrowed. What was dark. Which verb for their test. Rooms not entered. A note written the next afternoon from memory will promote the rooms you understood and drop the door that stayed shut. The shut door is the point of writing it the same day.

Do not add serials to that note if the note will be pasted into the opinion. Function and result are enough. Their asset file already has the identities. A working note that only makes sense beside a photograph is a caption. Rewrite it in sentences before you leave the building, while you can still check a door.

If they ask for a verbal result at the door, give the limits, not a preview of the yes. "Count done, one identity gap, performance not witnessed, second feed spoken only." That is a complete door sentence. "Looks fine" is the sentence you will spend the next week taking back.

## Statistical Field Sampling Mathematics: Count, Identify, Sample, Witness

In institutional M&A acquisitions and project finance underwriting for mission-critical data centers, every qualitative observation recorded during the site walk must be translated into a deterministic commercial or contractual parameter for the investment committee and lending syndicate:

$$n_{\text{sample}} = \lceil \sqrt{N_{\text{population}}} \rceil + 1$$

An observation that merely remarks on plant appearance without quantifying its impact on **Firm Deliverable IT Capacity ($\text{MW}$)**, **Single-Point-of-Failure ($\text{SPOF}$) Availability**, **Immediate Catch-Up Capital Expenditure ($\text{CapEx}$)**, or **Conditions Precedent ($\text{CP}$) / Conditions Subsequent ($\text{CS}$)** fails to protect the relying party.

| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Primary Audit Objective** | Statistical Field Sampling Mathematics: Count, Identify, Sample, Witness | Cross-check VDR contracts against physical nameplates & test logs | Convert unverified claims into explicit CP/CS or valuation haircuts |
| **Sampling & Evidence Rule** | Curated tour of flagship hall or summary slide | Statistical random sample ($n = \lceil\sqrt{N}\rceil + 1$) chosen by auditor | Any sample mismatch triggers expanded $100\%$ population audit |
| **Redundancy & Capacity Gate** | Nameplate sum of generators, chillers, or transformers | Derate for $99.6\%$ ASHRAE extreme wet-bulb and N+1/2N fault paths | Lock underwritten revenue model to firm derated MW ceiling |
| **Financial Protection Mechanism** | Seller warranty representation in purchase agreement | Quantify remediation cost $C_{\text{fix}}$ + schedule delay risk | Require $150\%\text{--}200\%$ cash escrow holdback at financial close |

## PROTOCOL: A spare is evidence. A failure probability is not.
- Canonical URL: https://datacenterfieldguides.com/blog/spare-not-a-probability
- Raw Markdown URL: https://datacenterfieldguides.com/raw/spare-not-a-probability.md
- Volume: Volume 09 (Walk a TDD: Technical Due Diligence Physical Site Audit)
- Primary Keyword / Scope: data center critical spares vs MTBF probability TDD

# A spare is evidence. A failure probability is not.

> **Direct Answer Block**: Why theoretical vendor MTBF probabilities cannot substitute for physical on-shelf critical spares (breaker coils, VFD igbts, CDU seals) during a Technical Due Diligence audit. In mission-critical data center commissioning and operations, engineers enforce this boundary using deterministic physical equations, calibrated field instrumentation, and auditable sign-off gates rather than relying on vendor brochure summaries, uncalibrated software plots, or verbal assurances. Every measurement and state transition must be recorded with synchronized UTC timestamps and explicit pass/fail thresholds before a signature is granted.

![Spare, person, stop. Not a probability.](figures/flagship/fig-02-utility-substation-and-grid-diversity.png)

A small calculated chance that several machines fail together looks like engineering. It is a story, unless the failure figure comes from a document you may cite, for this equipment, and you are allowed to use it. A figure half remembered from "industry practice" is not that document. The product will be quoted as your judgment that simultaneous failure can be ignored.

The check that belongs in the opinion is ordinary. Is there a spare for the failure the contract assumes, on a shelf a second person can find, or only on a list. Is there a person on the roster for the hour that matters, and can that person say the first safe state without the binder. Is the emergency paper short enough to be that stop, or is it a repair manual. Seen, documented, or only spoken. Spoken does not enter the opinion as tested.

Redundancy on a slide is the same trap. Two feeds drawn are not two feeds tested. A generator brochure runtime is not a test. Design kilowatts are not tonight's load. Do not add them to look complete. Do not fill the gap with a probability.

If any of the practical checks is missing, the service level is not evidenced. You do not need a tiny number to say that. A tiny number would hide it.

## 2. Deep-Dive Technical Protocol and Field Implementation

The following field protocol—adapted directly from **Volume 09: *Walk a TDD: Technical Due Diligence Physical Site Audit***—establishes the step-by-step verification mechanics required on the data hall floor:

A plant does not meet a service level because the equipment is redundant on a slide. It meets it if someone is there, the stop is findable, and the part the job refuses to start without is in a place a second person can find.

The roster is a document, not a name they mention. Who covers the hour the contract cares about. A team name is not a person. If the roster and the interview disagree, write both. Do not pick the kinder one.

Training is a signature that the pages were shown, not a slide attendance sheet, if they claim the staff can run the platform.

Maintenance policy and lifespan are claims about the future. You may note the manufacturer's stated life if a document says it, and you say you did not test the life. You may not convert a depreciation period in a contract into a technical life. Those are different sentences. Counsel owns the first. You refuse to dress it as the second.

## 3. Field Verification Checklist and Instrumentation Hygiene

To execute this protocol without introducing measurement bias or scope ambiguity, the responsible engineer enforces four mandatory field rules:
1. **Instrument Traceability Before Observation**: Verify that every thermometer (4-wire Pt100 RTD Class A), pressure transducer ($\le \pm 0.1\%$ span), flowmeter, balometer, or power analyzer carries a current calibration certificate and passes a pre-test zero/span check on the day of the walk.
2. **Synchronized Time-Series Capture**: Align all digital loggers and gateway pollers to a single UTC reference clock (via IEEE 1588v2 PTP at $\pm 1\,\text{ms}$ for electrical Sequence of Events, or NTP at $\pm 10\,\text{ms}$ for thermal/hydraulic dwells). Never merge unsynchronized CSV files by row index.
3. **Explicit Isolation of Disturbances vs. Control Handles**: Hold upstream supply temperatures, parallel cabinet loads, and containment door states constant during the observation dwell so that transient plant drift is never mistaken for steady-state equipment performance.
4. **Written Record Prior to Signature**: Record every boundary tag, measured value, uncertainty tolerance, and open limitation in ink on the controlled project sheet before leaving the equipment line-up.

---

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

### Why does "A spare is evidence. A failure probability is not." matter during high-density data center commissioning and operations?
Why theoretical vendor MTBF probabilities cannot substitute for physical on-shelf critical spares (breaker coils, VFD igbts, CDU seals) during a Technical Due Diligence audit. When project teams bypass this rule to meet a commercial schedule milestone, unverified physical assumptions—such as hidden hydraulic pressure drops, unlogged polling gaps, unblanked bypass leakage, or uncalibrated sensor offsets—transfer directly into live 24/7 production as latent single points of failure.

### How do you quantitatively verify compliance with "data center critical spares vs MTBF probability TDD" on the physical floor?
Compliance is verified by executing the governing mathematical balance ($$\text{MTTR}_{\text{without\_spare}} = t_{\text{OEM\_lead\_time}} \gg \tau_{\text{redundancy\_survival}}$$) using independent, calibrated field instruments across a stabilized steady-state dwell window (minimum 15 to 30 minutes for thermal and hydraulic systems), and confirming that the discrepancy between primary and secondary measurements remains strictly within the pre-declared acceptance band.

### What should an engineer do if a contractor or vendor submits a report that violates this protocol?
The reviewing engineer must refuse to sign the broad acceptance sentence, mark the specific line item as **Unproved / Defective** on the official audit sheet, and either require a witnessed re-test under a corrected script or isolate the unproved scope under a time-bounded Conditional Acceptance with a $150\%$ to $200\%$ financial retainage escrow holdback.

## PROTOCOL: A data center TDD is not a commissioning
- Canonical URL: https://datacenterfieldguides.com/blog/tdd-is-not-a-commissioning

# A data center TDD is not a commissioning

> **Direct Answer Block**: Understanding the structural difference between a buyer/lender Technical Due Diligence (TDD) risk audit and an ASHRAE Level 1–5 commissioning execution. In mission-critical data center commissioning and operations, engineers enforce this boundary using deterministic physical equations, calibrated field instrumentation, and auditable sign-off gates rather than relying on vendor brochure summaries, uncalibrated software plots, or verbal assurances. Every measurement and state transition must be recorded with synchronized UTC timestamps and explicit pass/fail thresholds before a signature is granted.

![Scope, chairs, and the sentence](figures/flagship/fig-03-natural-hazards-and-flood-plain-hydrology.png)

A technical due diligence is a reading of risk against a contract, by someone who will not own the plant and will not operate it. The reader is a lender or a buyer. They need to know whether the papers' assumptions are evidenced. They do not need a second design, and they do not need a certificate that the hall was commissioned.

You do not issue levels. You may read a level map if one exists and say whether the words match the tests. You do not rerun the heat window. You do not audit the tenant's applications because a dashboard was on. Scope is a line written before the questionnaire: which layer is in, which layer is out. Crossing the line feels thorough. It makes the report wider than the access you had.

Three chairs stay separate. Someone provides the room. Someone operates the equipment put in the room. Someone specified it and may run the work. A service level often assumes all three. One chair's confidence does not clear another's missing test. Market language, a competitiveness adjective, a forecast, are not findings. If the engagement forces a market section, label it not a finding, and do not let the opinion cite it.

The sentence you sign is narrow, and the limits sit in the same section. A yes without the limits will be quoted without them.

---

## 1. First-Principles Engineering Formulation and Governing Mathematics

In high-density data center environments, verbal summaries and qualitative status tiles routinely obscure incipient physical failures. Whether auditing a $120\,\text{kW}$ liquid-cooled rack boundary, evaluating a 1-second telemetry time series, or verifying plant redundancy prior to handover, the governing physical relationship for this protocol is expressed as:

$$\text{TDD Verdict} = \{\text{Tier 1 Fatal Flaws}, \text{Firm Derated MW}, \text{CP/CS Covenants}, \text{CapEx Reserve}\}$$

When any term on the left-hand or right-hand side of this relationship is left unmeasured, inferred from an uncalibrated nameplate, or averaged across an unverified time window, the resulting engineering record cannot support a valid operational signature. Field engineers must verify each physical variable independently using NIST/ISO 17025 traceable instruments before proceeding to the next gate in the sequence.

| Audit Verification Parameter | Unacceptable / Defective Field Practice | Auditable First-Principles Requirement | Mandatory Action on Failure |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Primary Boundary Definition** | Implied by vendor brochure or slide deck | Explicitly bounded on stamped P&ID / SLD with tag IDs | Halt acceptance; issue formal boundary clarification |
| **Measurement & Telemetry Proof** | Single uncalibrated display reading or 60-sec average | Calibrated Class A/0.5S sensor with 1-sec UTC timestamp | Reject dataset; classify point as `0x40` Stale or `0x80` Bad |
| **Pass / Fail Acceptance Gate** | Qualitative "Looks OK" or "Within Normal Range" | Quantitative numerical corridor cited from revision in force | Log Category A/B defect; withhold retainage or permit |
| **Custody & Sign-Off Record** | Single bundled "Accepted" signature at end of meeting | Scoped, dated sentence naming exact proved & unproved lines | Strike unsupported claims; issue Conditional Refusal |

---

## 2. Deep-Dive Technical Protocol and Field Implementation

The following field protocol—adapted directly from **Volume 09: *Walk a TDD: Technical Due Diligence Physical Site Audit***—establishes the step-by-step verification mechanics required on the data hall floor:

A technical due diligence is a reading of technical risk against a contract, done by someone who does not own the plant and will not operate it. The reader is usually a lender, sometimes a buyer. They need to know whether the thing they are financing can do the job the papers say, and what happens if a named assumption fails. They do not need a second design, and they do not need you to be enthusiastic.

Three principles are enough. You are independent of the parties. You follow risk to a delivery node or to later operation, not every interesting detail. You check compliance by citing the title the contract already names, not by pasting the standard. If a finding does not change a delivery date, a contracted performance, a permit, or the ability to operate, it is a note. Notes may be filed. They do not get the tone of a red flag.

You will be asked to certify things the financing documents name. Read that list before you travel. A certification you did not see in the engagement is not yours to invent on site. A certification you cannot evidence is refused, in the same document as any yes. The handover book already required that shape. It applies here with a lender in the room instead of an operator.

## What the visit is not

It is not a market essay. A paragraph about regional demand, geopolitics, or how competitive the platform "feels" is not a technical finding. If the engagement asks for obsolescence risk, you write what the contract assumes about the equipment generation, and whether a supply agreement covers a shortfall. You do not write a forecast. Counsel reads the warranty. You say whether the technical assumption inside it is evidenced.

It is not a commissioning. You do not issue levels. You may read a level map if one exists, and say whether the words match the tests. The third book owns how those levels are numbered. You do not reteach them in the lender's report.

It is not a safety inspection you are not qualified to sign, and it is not a legal opinion. Permits are confirmed with counsel, from the documents they accept. You do not bless a filing because the cover looks official.

## The four-stage review and the risk taxonomy

Every technical due diligence operates along a disciplined four-stage pipeline. Conflating stages or delivering an informal verdict at the curb destroys the legal insulation of the technical opinion:

1. **Stage 1: Desk Review and Virtual Data Room (VDR) Audit**: Inspect utility interconnection agreements, firm capacity reservations, Single-Line Diagrams (SLD), civil hydrology studies, building permits, Certificate of Occupancy, Phase I Environmental Site Assessments (ESA), and equipment maintenance logs.
2. **Stage 2: Physical Site Walk and Asset Verification**: Execute the four core acts—Count against inventory, sample identity under the pre-written rule (N_sample = √N + 1), sample running operational state, and verify test documentation without confusing pass certificates with witnessed tests.
3. **Stage 3: Interim Red-Flag Report (48-Hour Turnaround)**: Deliver an early, numbered ledger identifying deal-breakers, unmitigated single points of failure (SPOF), and material capital expenditure (CAPEX) catch-up requirements.
4. **Stage 4: Final Technical Opinion and Financing Covenants**: Formulate enforceable Conditions Precedent (CP) required prior to initial debt drawdown, Conditions Subsequent (CS) post-closing cure milestones, and formal escrow holdbacks (150%–200% of remediation cost).


Findings are rigorously segregated into a three-tier hierarchy:
- **Tier 1: Fatal Flaw (Red Flag)**: Unresolvable utility clawbacks, location within unmitigated 100-year/500-year flood plains, lack of fundamental zoning or occupancy permits, unresolvable right-of-way encumbrances, or total absence of emergency autonomous run paths. Halts debt syndication immediately.
- **Tier 2: Material Deficiency (Amber Flag)**: Degraded fuel without polishing, floor loading deficits for dense AI racks, single-header cooling vulnerabilities, or incomplete integrated systems commissioning. Handled via mandatory Conditions Precedent and financial escrow holdbacks.
- **Tier 3: Operational Defect (Green Flag)**: Redline drawing reconciliation backlog, minor maintenance contract renewal gaps, or cosmetic non-structural defects. Resolved under Conditions Subsequent within a 90-day post-closing cure window.

## Quantitative Risk Scoring and Deal-Breaker Thresholds in Technical Due Diligence

During Stage 1 through Stage 4 of the Technical Due Diligence, every physical observation is scored against its unmitigated Single-Point-of-Failure ($\text{SPOF}$) probability and capital remediation cost ($C_{\text{remedy}}$):

$$\text{Risk Exposure}_{k} = P_{\text{failure}, k} \times \left( C_{\text{SLA\_penalty}} + C_{\text{remedy}, k} \right)$$

| TDD Risk Classification Tier | Technical Trigger Criterion | Required Financial / Legal Covenant Action | Sign-Off Owner |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Tier 1: Fatal Flaw (Red Flag)** | Unmitigated 500-yr flood plain, missing grid easement, structural slab overload | Immediate halt to debt drawdown / deal exclusivity | Investment Committee |
| **Tier 2: Material Deficiency (Amber)** | N+1 cooling shortfall at $99.6\%$ wet-bulb, unpolished fuel, missing IST | Mandatory Condition Precedent (CP) + $150\%\text{--}200\%$ Cash Escrow | Lead Technical Advisor + Counsel |
| **Tier 3: Operational Defect (Green)** | As-built redline backlog, minor PM log gaps, cosmetic seal wear | Condition Subsequent (CS) cured within $90\,\text{days}$ post-close | Asset Management / Operations |
